sections.h2: Sales routes for a Philadelphia homeowner
sections.html:
Most Philadelphia owners pick from three paths: an agent, a sale by owner, or a cash buyer. Each ends at the Department of Records with a recorded deed and the city's transfer tax. The difference lies in timing, repairs and what you walk away with.

The city is also its own county. Philadelphia and Philadelphia County have shared one government since 1854, so the assessment office, the tax collector and the deed recorder are all city departments, and no outside courthouse comes into a typical sale.

  • A listing works for a rowhouse in good shape that can sit through weeks of showings while a buyer's loan is approved.
  • Going it alone saves the commission, though you handle the contract and settlement details yourself.
  • Cash fits deferred repairs, a clouded title, a tenant in the house or an estate being closed out.

The largest single cost the city sets is the realty transfer tax. Since July 1, 2025 the combined rate has been 4.578%, made up of 3.578% for the city and 1% for the Commonwealth. The rate had last changed in 2018, and the increase is earmarked for affordable housing programs.

Your sales agreement assigns the cost, so check that clause first. The tax is due when the deed is recorded. The city allows up to 30 days after the purchase, yet the Department of Revenue advises settling it at closing, and the Philadelphia Tax Center takes online payment.

When there is no sale price, such as a transfer between relatives, the tax is figured on the value the Office of Property Assessment has set for the property.

Deeds to a spouse, child or grandchild escape the tax, as do transfers under a will. Each family exemption must be backed by papers filed with the deed. Collect them before settlement rather than counting on the settlement agent to do it.

Estates trip up many families. The house passes tax-free to the heirs under the will, but a later sale by those heirs to a buyer is taxed. If you inherited a Philadelphia house and plan to sell, budget for the full rate at that second step.

The city had an estimated 1,574,281 residents in July 2025, down about 1.8% from April 2020. Most of the housing stock dates to the 18th, 19th and early 20th centuries. Federal-style blocks stand in Old City and Society Hill, Victorian homes fill North Philadelphia, and twin houses are common in West Philadelphia. A buyer or investor looking at an older rowhouse will price in the roof, the party walls and the plumbing, which is why condition drives offers more here than in newer suburbs.

  • The middle home value for owners is $243,100 in the 2020 to 2024 figures, with 51.8% of households owning.
  • Rent runs a median $1,397 a month across 679,428 households of 2.26 people on average.
  • Commutes average 31.7 minutes.

sections.h2: Property taxes and the Homestead Exemption
sections.html:
The Office of Property Assessment sets values, and the Department of Revenue bills them. Bills go out each December 1, new assessments take effect January 1, and payment is due March 31. Ask the Office of Property Assessment how to dispute a value, since the review deadlines fall in early fall each year.

The Homestead Exemption takes $100,000 off the taxable portion of an owner-occupied home's assessed value, and most owners save $1,399 a year. A mortgage or delinquent taxes leave eligibility intact, while a 10-year abatement rules it out. An accepted application keeps working until the deed changes, so a buyer who will live in the house files their own application. The final date to apply is December 1 each year, and applying by October 1 puts the credit on the first bill.

  • An heir without their name on the deed can ask for a conditional Homestead Exemption, granted for up to three years, using a paper application marked Tangled Title.
  • Seniors and income-qualified owners can pay in eleven monthly installments if they apply by March 31.
  • The owner-occupied payment agreement can set a monthly payment as low as zero for past-due tax.

For a house with back taxes, ask the Department of Revenue for a payoff figure before you accept an offer, because delinquent tax is paid from the proceeds.

Chapter 73 of Title 68, the Real Estate Seller Disclosure Law, calls for a signed statement about known defects, handed over before any agreement of transfer is signed. Seventeen subjects appear on the form, among them the roof, basement, wiring, drainage and title questions. Nothing forces you to hire testers, yet you cannot assert what you know is untrue.

Act 74 adds section 7305.2, a flood insurance notice that goes to the buyer once the Insurance Department publishes its flood information page. Suits over a violation must start within two years of final settlement, and an executor selling for an estate stands outside the chapter.

Two records decide how fast a closing moves: the deed and the tax account. The city's property search shows the assessed value, any homestead credit and the balance owed, while the deed tells you who has to sign.

  • Collect the deed, your latest bill and a lender payoff letter if you have a mortgage.
  • Keep papers proving family relationships if the transfer could be exempt.
  • Compare each repair with what it would add to your price.
  • Agree on the transfer tax split in writing, whoever the buyer is.

Any buyer worth talking to will explain the tax, the recording charge and the payoff up front and let you say no.

The signing is brief. You execute the deed, the transfer tax and recording charge are paid, and the title company deducts your mortgage payoff and any past-due tax before wiring the rest. Without a lender in the deal, timing hinges on how fast the title search and payoff figures arrive. When the buyer needs a loan, the lender controls part of the calendar.

Inherited houses need the will paperwork in hand. With a tenant in place, set the move-out date in writing so closing isn't left to chance.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax rate for a Philadelphia house sale?
faqs.a: The rate is 4.578%, made of 3.578% for the city and 1% for the Commonwealth, and it has applied since July 1, 2025. It is figured on the price, or on the assessed value if no price exists. The contract says who pays.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell an inherited house in Philadelphia?
faqs.a: Yes. The passing of the house under a will is exempt from transfer tax, but when the heirs sell to an outside buyer that sale is taxed. An heir whose name is missing from the deed may request a conditional Homestead Exemption lasting up to three years.

faqs.q: Does the Homestead Exemption pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: No, a buyer who will live in the home applies separately, since an accepted application lasts only until the deed changes. December 1 is the yearly cutoff, and October 1 is the date that gets the credit onto the first bill.

faqs.q: When is the Philadelphia real estate tax due?
faqs.a: March 31. Bills are mailed from December 1 of the prior year. Seniors and income-qualified owners may spread payment over eleven monthly installments by applying before March 31.

faqs.q: What if a Philadelphia seller omits a known defect?
faqs.a: The seller can owe the buyer actual damages. A buyer may sue a seller who willfully or negligently breaks the disclosure duties, with the case filed inside two years of final settlement.
